title: Adjustment Disorder - Criteria and Core Features
content:
DOCUMENT TYPE: Criteria

CORE ALIASES: Adjustment disorder, situational depression, stress reaction, reactive distress.

DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA:
A. The development of emotional or behavioral symptoms in response to an identifiable stressor(s) occurring within 3 months of the onset of the stressor(s).
B. These symptoms or behaviors are clinically significant as evidenced by one or both of the following:
1. Marked distress that is out of proportion to the severity or intensity of the stressor, taking into account the external context and cultural factors that might influence symptom severity and presentation.
2. Significant impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning.
C. The stress-related disturbance does not meet the criteria for another mental disorder and is not merely an exacerbation of a preexisting mental disorder.
D. The symptoms do not represent normal bereavement.
E. Once the stressor or its consequences have terminated, the symptoms do not persist for more than an additional 6 months.

REQUIRED FEATURES: Identifiable psychosocial stressor (loss, change, conflict, medical illness, work problem). Onset within 3 months. Distress or impairment out of proportion. Not better explained by another disorder.

RULE-OUTS / DIFFERENTIALS: Major Depressive Disorder (if criteria for MDD met, diagnose MDD instead), PTSD (requires trauma exposure meeting Criterion A and specific symptom clusters), Generalized Anxiety Disorder (excessive worry not tied to single stressor), Normal bereavement, Acute Stress Disorder.

COMMON COMORBIDITIES: MDD, GAD, Substance Use Disorders, Sleep Disorders.

PROVENANCE: DSM-5-TR criteria. Guideline summary: APA practice guideline emphasizes time-limited nature and stressor linkage. Systematic review: Symptoms typically resolve with resolution of stressor or with brief intervention.
